subject: Localized case study + translation rights in exchange for multi-year commitment
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@solsticehealth.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: localized case study + translation rights for multi-year commit

Hi Ana / Miguel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, Solstice’s story (clinical outcomes + cost savings) would make a strong case study for us and we’d love to collaborate on a localized version for your global teams. I’ve attached a short brief with proposed talking points and examples.

To move forward faster, the deal team is willing to offer a pricing concession tied to the case study + translation/localization rights. Proposed exchange:

- Customer commits to a 3-year term (minimum annual committed spend to be defined in the MSA).
- Redwood provides a one-time 22% off list pricing year-1 for committed capacity (applies to committed ARR only).
- Solstice grants Redwood non-exclusive rights to publish a localized case study in English + Spanish + French, and allows Redwood to use translated excerpts in marketing (web, slide decks, regional events).
- Public release will observe an embargo window — proposed 60 days after final sign-off from both parties.

Please review and let me know whether translation rights and the 3-year commit are acceptable. If so, we’ll route a short amendment (Exhibit A) to capture the scope and release windows.

Attachments: Solstice_CaseStudy_Brief.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference
From: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@solsticehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Solstice Legal <legal@solsticehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: localized case study + translation rights for multi-year commit

Mina —

Appreciate the thoughtful proposal. We like the idea, but a few asks from our side before we agree to any exchange:

- Translation/localization rights: We want to ensure our translations are managed by our preferred vendor. Can Redwood permit us to provide translated copy and grant Redwood a right to use Solstice-supplied translations (rather than Redwood commissioning translations)?
- Exclusivity: We cannot grant exclusive rights to translations; any rights must be non-exclusive and limited to the assets described in the brief.
- Discount: 22% is close but we need 25% year-1 to justify the commit to our procurement and budget committee.
- Logo and trademark use: Must be reviewed by our brand team and limited to agreed lockups.

Looping in Solstice Legal for redlines. I’ve attached a short doc with our brand/translation requirements. If Redwood can accept non-exclusive, allow Solstice-managed translations, and confirm logo lockups, we’ll escalate to procurement this week.

Attachment: solstice_requirements.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Miguel
Head of Partnerships, Solstice Health
miguel.torres@solsticehealth.com

Team — FYI and seeking approval. Solstice is asking for: 1) permission to supply translations (they want us to accept Solstice-provided localized copy), 2) 25% off year-1, and 3) brand lockup review.

Context: this is a net-new enterprise opportunity with strong references across several large hospital systems. Procurement wants a clear incentive to sign the 3-year committed capacity.

Requesting quick guidance on whether we can:
- Accept Solstice-supplied translations and agree in the amendment to use their translated copy (we'd still get final sign-off on any localized marketing creative).
- Move from 22% to 25% year-1 if we secure a signed 3-year commitment and a minimum committed ARR threshold.

Jonas — can marketing own the creative review + lockup approval? Marissa — can legal draft a short Exhibit A that:
- Confirms non-exclusive, non-transferable rights for Redwood to publish a localized case study using Solstice-supplied translations,
- Limits trademark/logo use to agreed lockups, and
- Sets the publicity embargo window (they propose 60 days; legal can counter).

Thanks — this is time-sensitive; Miguel said procurement will escalate this week.

— Mina

Mina — thanks for the flag. I’m comfortable approving a concession with the following conditions:

- Approved concession: up to 22% off year-1 list pricing for committed ARR on a signed 3-year commitment.
- We can stretch to 25% only if: customer agrees to a minimum committed ARR (proposed $600k ARR) and provides written confirmation that translations will be provided by Solstice and cleared by our marketing team within 14 business days of artwork delivery.
- Non-exclusive, non-transferable license is required for localized materials; no perpetual transfer of IP.
- Embargo window to be 45 days post final sign-off (compromise between our hope for earlier promotion and their 60-day ask).
- Marketing (Jonas) to own lockup review and will send a small checklist for brand approvals.
- Legal (Marissa) to draft an amendment and flag any IP issues.

If Solstice accepts the ARR floor and the 45-day embargo, we can finalize this via a short amendment and route for signature. Vivek — please note for deal desk reporting.

Vanessa Ortiz

Team —

I drafted a short Exhibit A to capture the agreed points; attaching the draft for review (redwood-draft-exhibit-A.docx). Key legal positions included inline below — please confirm so I can prepare the amendment for signature via DocuSign:

1) License scope: Non-exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide license to use the specified case study assets in English, Spanish, and French, including customer-supplied translations. Redwood’s right to use customer-provided translations is conditioned on Solstice warranting translation accuracy and granting Redwood the right to publish.

2) IP/trademark: Solstice retains trademark and logo ownership; Redwood will use logo only per mutually approved lockups. Marketing to use the checklist and return approvals within 10 business days.

3) Embargo: Agreed 45-day embargo after final sign-off.

4) Exclusivity: No exclusivity for translations; customer may license translations to third parties.

5) Consideration: The pricing concession (22% off year-1 list) applies to committed ARR only and is contingent on a signed 3-year commitment and a minimum committed ARR of $600,000.

If you approve, I’ll upload to DocuSign and include the HubSpot deal link. One legal note: if the customer insists on 25% without the ARR floor, require CS/finance to model impact before approval.

Attachment: redwood-draft-exhibit-A.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
